_note: Characters and court (game-design §4; docs/v1-content.md §2). One turn is one year. PLACEHOLDER numbers throughout.

aging._note: Ages 0 to child_until move child_years_per_turn per turn; then one year per turn through the formative years (the career is chosen before formative_until); adults age one year per turn until prime, then stop (game-design §4.2: no old age, no sickness).

warlord.name: Warlord
warlord.text: A single-entity champion: duels and lord-killing (map actions come with agents).

assassin.name: Assassin
assassin.text: Wounds and kills characters, sabotages (map actions come with agents).

spy.name: Spy
spy.text: Intelligence, rumours and forged letters (map actions come with agents).

merchant.name: Merchant
merchant.text: Trade deals, secret funding and smuggling (map actions come with agents).

wizard.name: Wizard
wizard.text: Campaign spells and battle magic (map actions come with agents).

priest.name: Priest
priest.text: Church influence and the faith (map actions come with agents).

xp._note: Experience: every adult earns per_turn of its career's work each turn, deeds add more (data/traits.json deeds). The level needed for xp is level_xp x (level - 1) ^ level_power, with no cap; one skill point per level. Generals level from battle experience as before (their army's rank). immortal_level: a character who reaches it becomes immortal; a defeated immortal returns after return_defeated turns (game-design §4.5).

births._note: A married couple with both adults (age 18-45 for the mother) has a child with chance per turn, up to max_children together. Children take the father's race and culture (game-design §4.9). No one dies of old age, so births pause while the court has max_court living members (keeps courts and End Turn bounded; a placeholder until deaths, schemes and marriages out thin courts).
births._soft_note: Soft cap (owner spec 2026-10-07): a court's size cap rises with Realm Standing from court_cap[0] at the lowest level to court_cap[1] at the highest; the birth chance falls as the court fills (x (1 - members/cap)^slow), reaching nothing at the cap.

courtiers._note: Lesser nobles and adventurers ask to join a powerful or famous court: chance per turn x Realm Standing level, while the court has fewer than max members.

loyalty._note: One visible loyalty per character, 0-100, every change logged with its reason (game-design §4.6). start: a family member's starting loyalty; courtiers and absorbed families start lower. Neglect: an adult with no role, title or gift for neglect_after turns loses neglect_loss a turn. Favouritism: when one branch (a child of the ruler and their descendants) holds favouritism_share or more of the court's roles, every other branch loses favouritism_loss a turn. gift_per: loyalty per gift_gold gold given.

marriage._note: Adults of age 16+ who are unmarried may marry, within a faction or across (a cross-faction marriage is also a diplomatic item). The spouse joins the husband's court unless married into the wife's ruling family (matrilineal when the wife is the ruler or heir). Cross-race allowed; children take the father's race.

family._note: Generated family to fill out each house at the start (founders and named lords from the world bible and docs/v1-content.md; everyone else generated from the culture's name pools, PLACEHOLDER): a spouse, children_min-children_max children aged 1-17, siblings_min-siblings_max adult siblings, and courtiers_min-courtiers_max courtiers for major and playable houses (minor houses get fewer).
